purpose: The real source, load order and failure mode of every Lua file the isolated AI runtime depends on. Authored by hand, enforced by tools/ai/check-ai-runtime-manifest.py so drift fails a test instead of surfacing as a dead AI in a fresh deployment.
why_no_hashes: lua/ai/ is not version-controlled in this repository (.gitignore:11) and the fetcher default ref is a moving branch, so a content hash here would be stale on the next upstream push. The one pinned hash that does exist stays in docs/lua-ai-spec.md, next to the patch that produces it. This manifest pins presence, order and gates, not bytes.

upstream.ref_pinned_note: Not pinned: QSAN_EXTENSIONS_REF defaults to main. The local synchronized checkpoint is recorded below; publishing or choosing a fixed CI ref is a separate operation.

local_modification.change: Both fetchers sed the AI load loop from "lua/ai/"..sl to "lua/ai/"..ai_file, working around an upstream bug that breaks mixed-case package AI on case-sensitive filesystems.
local_modification.consequence: The deployed file never matches upstream bytes. Its post-patch SHA-256 is recorded in docs/lua-ai-spec.md.

upstream.synced_note: Local external main checkpoint 6fcdfdd contains the isolated core scripts, facades and mode policy recorded below. This checkpoint is committed locally, not pushed; the remote default main does not yet deliver this checkpoint.
upstream.line_endings: ai/ is CRLF throughout; the fetcher copies bytes through unchanged.

version_control.consequence: A clean git clone of this repository contains no lua/ai/ at all. Because AiRouteRegistry::routeFor() defaults to AiRouteIsolated, AiLuaRuntime::initialize() then fails and no Room gets an AI runtime. Running a fetcher is a mandatory setup step, not an optimisation. The converse trap is just as real and cost this project a working upstream: because the tree is ignored, local edits to lua/ai/ are invisible to git status and can sit unpushed indefinitely, and the fetchers only copy - they never delete - so the machine that made them keeps working while every other environment is broken.
version_control.local_config_is_not_a_source: config.ini is gitignored. Anything that loads only because the local config.ini names it is absent from every other deployment, see files[].loaded_by_default.

load_chain.note: Removes dofile/require and the gameplay globals. Every later script must therefore be self-contained; none of them may pull a dependency in on its own.

Without an AiIsolatedScripts override the host loads ai_isolated_core as declared by isolated-bootstrap.lua (fatal on failure), then one <package>-ai.lua per enabled package (skipped on failure). An explicit AiIsolatedScripts is taken literally, empty list included; the isolation tests use it to stand up a runtime with one script or none.

isolated_core_scripts_note: Declared in the Lua tree, not in C++, so the list travels with the scripts it names. The host only carries it out, because the sandbox removes dofile. Order matters: ask-for-use-card.lua installs the handler registries the package handlers write into.
package_handler_rule: A package's isolated handlers load because that package is enabled and lua/ai/isolated/<package>-ai.lua exists, matched case-insensitively against Engine::getExtensions() - the same rule smart-ai.lua uses to find <package>-ai.lua in lua/ai. No host-side list names them, and a package without a handler file is the normal case. A handler that fails to load costs that package its isolated AI and nothing else.

files.role: Isolated VM bootstrap: handler registration, coverage declaration, the bounded not-covered log, ai_memory, and the ai_isolated_core declaration that says which dispatchers the host must load next. ai_decide is the one place an unsupported signal becomes a legacy fallback with a recorded reason.

files.role: Value-type facades: SmartAIView / PlayerView / CardView / CandidateView / AIList over the snapshot, the AIResultValue boundary, and AIUnsupported - the tagged signal that keeps 'not covered' apart from 'declined' and from a real error.

files.role: askForUseCard dispatcher; owns the pattern/skill handler registries for both callback ABIs.
Value-decision dispatcher: one registry per decision kind, keyed by request reason.

Shared decision flow: keep/use value, priority, sorting, threat assessment, turn candidates, the one target-ranking function every path uses, the aiUseCard / ai_card_use author API, and the first physical-card strategies (Slash, Peach).
Speech and response narration helpers used by the isolated decision dispatchers.
